I see that toolChoice propagates from defineAgent through PromptConfig into the generate options, so when it's set to 'required' the model must call a tool every turn—meaning after a decline it can't respond with text and just keeps calling tools until maxTurns is hit. I want to trace what happens after an interrupt resolves with approved:false to see how the model gets re-invoked.

The fix seems to be changing toolChoice from 'required' to 'auto' so the model can reply with plain text after a decline, matching how the triage agent is configured. I'm also wondering if the system prompt needs an added instruction telling the model to give the customer a short reply when a refund is declined, though the core bug looks like it's just that toolChoice line. I'd like to verify this empirically but I'm not sure I can run the app without an API key or network access, so I may need to rely on code inspection alone.

I should double-check whether toolChoice actually propagates from defineAgent through to genOpts and into the generate call, so I'm going to trace that path through prompt.ts and agent.ts to confirm the chain works as expected.
The agent loop calls `generateStream` with `genOpts` after an interrupt is resumed. I'll confirm `toolChoice` from the agent config actually reaches those options.

text:
I've traced the flow: defineAgent's toolChoice setting forces every model call to invoke a tool, including after a decline, so the model keeps calling tools like approveRefund or lookupOrder with no path to a final reply, eventually exhausting the 6-turn limit and failing. This points to a real interaction problem between forced tool choice and maxTurns.

The fix is to switch toolChoice to 'auto' so the model can reply with text after a decline. I'm weighing whether to also update the system prompt to explicitly instruct the model to stop and give a short reply when approval is declined, since relying solely on 'auto' might not guarantee the model stops calling approveRefund repeatedly given the current prompt wording.

I'll keep things minimal though and just make the toolChoice edit without running live verification, since I don't have access to the Genkit runtime here.

The path is confirmed: `defineAgent({ toolChoice })` flows into the agent's `generateStream` options on every turn. With `'required'`, the model cannot emit a plain-text reply after the supervisor declines, so it keeps calling tools until `maxTurns: 6` runs out. I'll change it to `'auto'`, the same setting the `triage` agent already uses.

The root cause is `toolChoice: 'required'` on `refundAgent` in `src/agents.ts`. I changed it to `'auto'`, the same setting `triage` already uses, and wrote `answer.json` in the project root.

With `'required'`, the model must call a tool on every turn. After the supervisor declines `approveRefund`, the model can't send a plain-text reply, so it keeps calling tools until `maxTurns: 6` runs out. That matches the reported re-asking for approval, continued order work, and failures.

I didn't run the flow against the live model because it needs an API key and the runtime. The typecheck showed no errors after the change. The evidence is from reading the Genkit source path that carries `toolChoice` into each agent turn.
